facts.raw_span: A 4-year-old boy presented with a 3-year history of nonhealing crusted scalp lesions
Previous treatments with various topical glucocorticosteroids and antibiotics showed no improvement
His mother reported occasional otitis media
The family history was negative for skin disease
Multiple disseminated erythematous papules, petechial hemorrhages, and yellowish crusts were present on the scalp
Neck, axillary, and inguinal lymph nodes showed no abnormalities
Routine blood examinations revealed no pathological findings
Two osteolytic lesions identified on the right frontoparietal skull
Subepidermal infiltrate consisting of large cells with kidney-shaped nuclei, solitary lymphocytes, and eosinophilic granulocytes
The infiltrate stained positively for CD1A
Ultrasonography of abdomen and lymph nodes: normal
Serum electrophoresis: normal

concepts.why: The presence of large cells with kidney-shaped nuclei, subepidermal infiltrate, and positive CD1A staining are characteristic of Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
The presence of erythematous papules, crusted scalp lesions, and negative family history of skin disease are consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus.
The presence of yellowish crusts, petechial hemorrhages, and eosinophilic granulocytes are characteristic of juvenile xanthogranuloma.
The presence of osteolytic lesions, large cells with kidney-shaped nuclei, and positive CD1A staining are consistent with eosinophilic granuloma.
The presence of nonhealing crusted scalp lesions, osteolytic lesions, and negative family history of skin disease are consistent with chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis.
The presence of erythematous papules, subepidermal infiltrate, and eosinophilic granulocytes are characteristic of histiocytoid Sweet syndrome.
The presence of nonhealing crusted scalp lesions, osteolytic lesions, and negative family history of skin disease are consistent with multicentric reticulohistiocytosis.
The presence of erythematous papules, subepidermal infiltrate, and large cells with kidney-shaped nuclei are characteristic of Rosai-Dorfman disease.
